own_analytical_findings.finding: Komekko visits a usual play place, calls the large stranger a big goblin, objects to kid address by giving her own name, acknowledges family warning and invokes a separate sister maxim against unreasonable demands. She asks what the not-a-goblin person is doing.
own_analytical_findings.limit: Do not assign the initial family warning to a specific parent or certify that she fully understands divine/sealing danger. The quoted maxim is her report of her sister, not a fresh witnessed Megumin instruction.

own_analytical_findings.finding: Native ホースト self-identification confirms Hoost/Horst retrieval identity. His rank/body/wing display receives her actual excited praise and raised hands. He makes a special exception to claimed witness-silencing practice and demands secrecy. She thanks while explicitly not understanding well, sits and explores the hard foot, then asserts the puzzle as her play possession.
own_analytical_findings.limit: Thanks is not established informed secrecy assent. No silencing attack, legal ownership judgment, unique calculated-flattery motive or global fearlessness is established.

own_analytical_findings.finding: She rapidly makes assembly progress; Hoost reports months of failure, takes the puzzle, and repeatedly fails to fit it to the pedestal. She objects to the taking. His favor-framed offer of play receives a hunger-based refusal/offloading reply; food promise and eventually deferential Komekko-san request precede her agreement. He departs to fetch food and she takes the puzzle again.
own_analytical_findings.limit: The three-page group does not yet perform the final sealing outcome or deliver food. Months is Hoost testimony. Food, changed request and respect are bundled; isolated status/food causation is not identified. Actual assembly progress is not a general IQ or universal puzzle/cosmic competence score.

actual_current_visual_receiving.title: こめっこさんとホースト様
actual_current_visual_receiving.source_plane: Komekko first-person integral image prose; reported background and actual current choices remain separate. No physical handwriting act is inferred.

own_analytical_findings.finding: A later visit continues the same seal problem. Komekko narrates that apparent first-puzzle completion disclosed a harder puzzle inside the pedestal. Hoost places an actual roasted chunk before her; hunting outside and inability to shop are his stated acquisition route. He asks about mother/friends.
own_analytical_findings.limit: No complete divine release is yet shown. More than one puzzle stage does not create independent psychological replications; exact elapsed visit count and meat species remain unestablished.

own_analytical_findings.finding: She reports mother usually absent, no same-age village friends and no toys, explaining this play choice. Hoost offers company until completion and occasional food, bounded by village security. Her stalled hands and repeated meat glances are visible in her account. He insists on progress-before-food, then explicitly resists her flattering coolness remark.
own_analytical_findings.limit: The family/social claims are her reported current perspective, not a neglect diagnosis, permanent friendlessness or a complete audit of parental care. Provider concern and task incentive coexist; no uniquely altruistic motive or unrestricted availability.

own_analytical_findings.finding: Her three-day no-solid/hard-food appeal is contradicted by his report of her finishing yesterday's hunted food. A future greater-than-sister mage threat also fails. A practical hunger/mental-work explanation plus polite food request precedes actual permission and her completion of the large salted portion. After eating she says she is sleepy and unmotivated, lies down but still handles the puzzle. Hoost changes to a polite Komekko-san plea; she gives a grudging acceptance that echoes his earlier phrase, and he explicitly acknowledges teaching it.
own_analytical_findings.limit: Do not turn the contradicted hardship appeal into certified starvation, general pathological dishonesty or proof of every unseen meal. Politeness, useful task framing, hunger and reciprocal face are bundled causes. Satiation does not produce sustained task compliance automatically; lying while handling the puzzle is not complete cessation. Final key placement/release or later progress remains unshown in these pages.

actual_current_visual_receiving.title: 紅魔族随一の魔性の妹
actual_current_visual_receiving.source_plane: Komekko first-person integral image prose. Decorative Megumin background is not a separate performed event or viewpoint; no physical writing act is inferred.

own_analytical_findings.finding: The second puzzle is solved and a third is revealed. Hoost rejects other Crimson Demons while excepting Komekko, then calls the third stage too difficult for a child. She cites her sister's reported maxim of doing what is called impossible and works lying down, kicking her feet and absorbed enough to ignore his cleaning her robe hem.
own_analytical_findings.limit: Success at two stages is specific task evidence, not general intelligence measurement, full seal completion or magical competence. Her quotation is reported teaching, not a newly witnessed sister choice.

own_analytical_findings.finding: Despite Hoost praising real progress, she puts the puzzle down and closes her eyes because she is bored. His offer to bring something tasty gets her up and working before delivery. When he prepares to hunt, she insistently asks to go and ride him, dismisses his monster warning by appealing to his apparent strength and praises him as cool. He ultimately takes her.
own_analytical_findings.limit: Boredom occurs during progress, not proven inability. Actual resumed work precedes the new food. Several appeals, novelty and recipient flattery are bundled; no uniquely isolated cause or guaranteed food-delivery outcome.

own_analytical_findings.finding: Hoost carries her to the forest and complains of her exuberant movement and near falling. She excitedly points out a large lizard to catch; he says her loud voice scared it away and explains other monsters flee his demon presence. She asks whether becoming strong would make monsters flee her too; he laughs off that possibility. A bush moves, apparently responding to his presence, and he sets her down. She asks if making that monster flee would mean she is stronger than him.
own_analytical_findings.limit: She explores strength through a concrete comparison and food/monster interest; no adult grasp of power rankings, no performed spell or confirmed superior strength. Hoost's account of ordinary monster flight is testimony distinct from the lizard's actual escape.

own_analytical_findings.finding: Hoost laughs at her comparison, warns that the hidden monster is frightening and asks whether its appearance would scare her into wetting herself. She rejects that outcome and volunteers to drive it away. He promises continued Komekko-san address if she succeeds. Multiple large bears emerge. While he judges the group troublesome and turns away to leave, she runs toward them with a hiss/shout; he cries out Komekko-san.
own_analytical_findings.limit: No bear defeat, bear flight, injury, rescue or completed return is shown at this group boundary. Running at the bears does not establish informed courage, reliable hazard calibration, a successful title bargain, combat power or a protective provider guarantee.

actual_current_visual_receiving.source_plane: Komekko first-person integral image prose; own actual conduct, Hoost exposition and unshown outcomes distinguished.

own_analytical_findings.finding: The puzzle has now been solved, but another requirement appears. Unable to read the displayed inscription, Komekko asks Hoost to read it. He proposes mutually dropping the honorific forms, which she accepts. He reads a hen and its child as altar offerings and a prayer but cannot read the ending; he initially treats it as a sacrifice to hunt.
own_analytical_findings.limit: Specific inability to read this inscription is not proof of total illiteracy or general incompetence. His partial reading and intended sacrifice are not a completed ritual or reliable theology. This page does not fill the earlier unshown bear outcome.

own_analytical_findings.finding: Hoost actually gives money and asks her to buy the best hen and child in the village. She returns after one hour with a covered bowl on a tray, calls it sacrificial oyakodon and carefully places it on the altar. Hoost checks and rejects this interpretation, saying the inscription cannot mean unlocking with oyakodon.
own_analytical_findings.limit: The actual item is a chicken-and-egg rice bowl. No evidence here establishes deliberate sabotage, an informed strategy to defeat Hoost's objective, money theft or a sexual meaning of the title. The failed offering and his expectation of meeting a half of Wolbach remain separate from actual release.

own_analytical_findings.finding: Komekko asks what sort of person Wolbach is. Hoost describes a huge jet-black magical beast and predicts she would be frightened. He says he must prepare the offering himself, will be absent for a while, asks secrecy, offers later play and explicitly lets her eat the bowl. After he flies away, she sits at the altar eating. Later a very small persistent beast emerges from the bushes and approaches her while she keeps eating.
own_analytical_findings.limit: Hoost's description and future promise are reported knowledge and intention, not independently verified true form, current huge-body appearance or performed return. The small animal is unnamed within this group; tiny appearance does not settle cosmic identity or power.

own_analytical_findings.finding: The small beast apparently seeks her bowl; she explicitly reasons that what Hoost has given her now belongs to her. She keeps eating standing up as it attacks, pulls at her legs and bites her head. After a long struggle it lies limp, still held against her with its head-bite maintained, and she declares victory and takes her trophy home.
own_analytical_findings.limit: This is actual food-retention persistence under interference and a specific struggle with a small beast, not generalized combat superiority, an adult risk calculation, demonstrated killing or an injury-free guarantee. No present new magical cast or confirmed final unsealing sequence is narrated here.

own_analytical_findings.finding: Hoost returns after an absence, carrying a cage with an actual large hen and chicks. He notices devastated surroundings and asks what happened. Komekko reports adults' claim that the revived evil god called an unnamed goddess to battle, lost and perished; Hoost drops his burden in dismay. She explicitly attributes that story to the adults, while her attention shifts to the birds.
own_analytical_findings.limit: The defeat/death is reported village knowledge, not a newly witnessed battle or trustworthy cosmology from the child. This report must not overwrite the distinct actual current meeting or fill the unshown precise release sequence.

own_analytical_findings.finding: Hoost reasons that his continuing presence contradicts his master's destruction and decides the half must still be alive somewhere and needs protection. He offers the now-unneeded birds to Komekko. She proposes the parent for dinner and chicks for Chomusuke; he objects on emotional-education grounds and takes the birds along instead. She offers to show a small jet-black beast; he declines, dismisses it as a kitten and dislikes its name.
own_analytical_findings.limit: No actual cooking, chick feeding or harm to birds is shown. His inferred survival and failure to inspect the small creature must not become omniscient identification. This group supplies her Chomusuke name and size description, but does not independently show the offered creature in front of Hoost.

own_analytical_findings.finding: She asks whether he is going away, appears displeased to him and nods to his explanation that he must find Wolbach. He predicts a promising magician, conditionally offers to become her familiar if his present contract ends and she can summon him, while stressing the difficulty. He lands, crouches to meet her eyes, says he senses devil-user aptitude and roughly rubs her head after her promise to try.
own_analytical_findings.limit: Future aptitude, contract release and summoning possibility are Hoost's appraisal and conditional promise, not performed magic, a new binding pact, verified future destiny or adult comprehension of contract terms.

own_analytical_findings.finding: They exchange stylized self-introductions. She names herself the house-sitter, the village's 魔性 little sister and Hoost's future intended master, taking a pose and throwing back her dragging cape. He laughs, flies outside the village, and she keeps waving until he is out of sight, explicitly calling him her first friend who often gave food despite his complaints.
own_analytical_findings.limit: The self-description is a child's persona and future boast, not adult sexual motive, proven power or accomplished service contract. Friendship and remembered provision coexist; neither cancels the other. No return or later success is performed here.
